analysis.summary: Brazil enter as clear favourites having topped Group C (W2 D1, 7 goals scored, 1 conceded) and edging Japan 2-1 late in the Round of 32. Norway finished second in Group I — thrashing Iraq 4-1 and beating Senegal 3-2 before a heavy 4-1 loss to France — then squeezed past Ivory Coast 2-1 courtesy of a late Haaland winner. The h2h hoodoo (Norway unbeaten in all 4 prior meetings including a 1998 World Cup upset) adds intrigue, but a significant quality gap and Brazil's superior defensive structure still make them comfortable favourites. Paqueta's tournament-ending thigh injury is the main concern for Brazil, while Haaland (five tournament goals) is Norway's primary threat.
analysis.home_form: Brazil topped Group C: drew 1-1 with Morocco (June 13), beat Haiti 3-0 (June 20) and Scotland 3-0 (June 24), then beat Japan 2-1 (Casemiro 56', Martinelli 90+5') in the Round of 32 on June 29. Attack led by Vinicius Jr. and Matheus Cunha; Alisson's defence conceded only once in 4 games. Manager: Carlo Ancelotti.
analysis.away_form: Norway won Group I runner-up spot: beat Iraq 4-1 (June 16), beat Senegal 3-2 (June 22), then lost 4-1 to France (June 26). Beat Ivory Coast 2-1 in Round of 32 (Nusa 39', Haaland 86') on June 30. Haaland has scored 5 goals in 4 tournament matches. Defense has conceded in every game (8 group-stage goals allowed, 1 in Round of 32).
analysis.h2h: Four all-time meetings; Norway unbeaten (W2 D2, L0). 1988: draw (friendly). 1997: Norway 4-2 Brazil (friendly). 1998: Norway 2-1 Brazil (1998 World Cup group stage — Rekdal penalty in 89'). 2006: 1-1 draw (friendly). Brazil have never beaten Norway in a competitive fixture, though all meetings predate the current generations.
injuries_news: Brazil — Lucas Paqueta: RULED OUT with thigh injury sustained in Japan match, expected to miss tournament unless Brazil reach final.
Brazil — Raphinha: doubtful (hamstring), has resumed individual training; may make bench.
Brazil — Neymar: could return to starting XI after playing only 14 minutes of the tournament.
Brazil — Casemiro: minor knock from Japan match but expected to feature.
Norway — Julian Ryerson: RULED OUT with thigh injury.
key_factors: Paqueta's absence removes Brazil's chief creative-midfield link; Ancelotti likely reshuffles to a more defensive midfield block.
Haaland (5 goals, all 4 Norway matches) is the single biggest danger — Brazil have no confirmed 'anti-Haaland plan' per Ancelotti's press conference.
Norway's defence has been porous all tournament (9 conceded in 4 games, BTTS in every match) — favours over-2.5 and BTTS outcomes.
Norway's historical unbeaten record against Brazil provides psychological edge but most meetings are over 16 years old.
MetLife is a closed dome; heat and altitude are non-factors, making a fluid, high-tempo game more likely.
Brazil have 5 days rest (beat Japan June 29); Norway have 4 days rest (beat Ivory Coast June 30) — minimal fatigue advantage.

My post-ET estimates: Brazil ~0.70, Norway ~0.30 — model is fractionally below market on both sides, so no h2h edge. Norway went over 2.5 total goals in 3 of 4 tournament matches; Brazil went over in 3 of 4; both attacks are genuine threats. Norway has recorded BTTS in all four tournament games including vs France; Brazil BTTS in both competitive-level matches (Morocco, Japan).
